fun_fact: Interstate 70 was one of the original highways in the Interstate Highway System, signed into law in 1956. It runs 2,153 miles from Cove Fort, Utah to Baltimore, Maryland.
why_tricky: Denver's I-70 corridor through the mountains looks similar to I-76 on a map — both run east from Denver, but I-76 heads northeast toward Nebraska while I-70 cuts west through the Rockies.

fun_fact: Interstate 90 is the longest Interstate Highway in the US at 3,020 miles, stretching from Seattle, WA to Boston, MA. It passes through Chicago as part of the Chicago Skyway.
why_tricky: I-90 and I-94 run concurrently through Chicago for several miles, making it hard to distinguish them on a regional map. The split happens on the north side of the city.

fun_fact: Interstate 10 through Houston contains the widest section of any highway in the world — the Katy Freeway has up to 26 lanes at its widest point.
why_tricky: Houston's highway network is extremely dense, and I-10 (the Katy Freeway) runs east-west through the city — easy to confuse with I-45 which slices through diagonally.

fun_fact: US Route 30, known as the Lincoln Highway in Pennsylvania, was part of America's first transcontinental highway. It passes through Gettysburg and Lancaster County.
why_tricky: Pennsylvania has several east-west US routes that look nearly identical on a map. US-30 and US-22 both run across the state and were both part of historic highway systems.

fun_fact: C-470 forms the southwest portion of Denver's beltway system, connecting I-70 near Golden to I-25 near Littleton. The eastern half of the loop is the toll road E-470.
why_tricky: Denver's beltway is split between E-470 (a toll road on the east/north) and C-470 (free, on the west/south) — confusing because they form one continuous loop but have different names and operators.

fun_fact: Interstate 5 is the West Coast's main north-south artery, running 1,381 miles from the Mexican border at San Diego to the Canadian border north of Blaine, WA.
why_tricky: Portland sits where I-5 meets I-84 — the junction is busy and the two interstates cross at the Marquam Bridge over the Willamette River.

fun_fact: I-80 follows roughly the same path as the historic Lincoln Highway and the Pony Express route across Nevada and Utah. The Bonneville Salt Flats lie just west of Salt Lake along I-80.
why_tricky: In Salt Lake, I-80 and I-15 intersect and both run through the valley — I-80 is the east-west route but the flat valley makes orientation difficult.

fun_fact: I-95 is the primary interstate along the Eastern Seaboard, running 1,920 miles from Fort Kent, Maine to Miami, Florida. It terminates at US-1 in downtown Miami.
why_tricky: South Florida has several north-south expressways including I-95, Florida's Turnpike, and US-1 running in parallel — they're easy to mix up on a regional map.

fun_fact: Route 66 earned the nickname 'The Mother Road' from John Steinbeck's The Grapes of Wrath. Oklahoma has the longest remaining driveable stretch of the original Route 66.
why_tricky: Through Oklahoma, Route 66 has been decommissioned and runs alongside I-40 for much of its path, making the original alignment hard to identify on modern maps.

fun_fact: Texas State Highway 130 (the Pickle Parkway) is a toll bypass around Austin with a posted speed limit of 85 mph — the highest legal speed limit on any road in the United States.
why_tricky: TX-130 loops east of Austin parallel to I-35, making it easy to confuse with I-35 or TX-45 on regional maps, especially since all three serve the Austin metro corridor.
